provenance.note: Anchor source for the slab tables, standard deduction, 87A rebate and surcharge structure, cross-checked against indiabudget.gov.in's Finance Bill memorandum and (for FY2026-27) the Income-tax Act 2025 statute text on indiankanoon.org — see citations for the entries sourced from those primaries directly.

regimes.new.slabs.note: Primary statute text: Section 202 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, in force from 1 April 2026, described there as 'similar to Section 115BAC' — same brackets, confirmed unchanged by Budget 2026 (Finance Act 2026 made no slab/rate changes; see https://www.businesstoday.in/personal-finance/tax/story/tax-slabs-fy-2026-27-what-budget-2026-changed-for-individual-taxpayers-and-which-regime-works-best-514044-2026-02-01 and https://cleartax.in/s/budget-2026-highlights).

regimes.new.standardDeduction.note: Primary statute text: Section 19 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 — '₹75000 ... where tax is computed under section 202(1); ₹50000 ... in any other case'.

regimes.new.rebate87A.note: Section 156 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (renumbered from old Section 87A) — 156(1) old-regime-equivalent (₹12,500/₹5L), 156(2) new-regime-equivalent (₹60,000/₹12L with marginal relief). Figures unchanged from FY2025-26.

regimes.old.section80cLimit.note: Section 80C renumbered to Section 123 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, from 1 April 2026 — limit unchanged at ₹1,50,000.

regimes.old.section24bSelfOccupiedCap.note: Primary statute text: Section 22 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (renumbered from old 24(b)) — Section 22(2)(a) '₹200000' for a qualifying self-occupied property, aggregate cap ₹200,000 under 22(5).

surcharge.slabs.note: Surcharge slabs/rates and the marginal-relief mechanism (excess tax vs excess income). Enhanced surcharge (25%/37%) is disapplied for dividend income and for gains taxed under 111A/112/112A (old Act) / 196/197/198 (new Act) — capped at 15% for those — see surcharge.capitalGainsCap.

hra.metroCities.note: OPEN QUESTION, not resolved: multiple secondary sources (TaxGuru, AngelOne, Greythr) report a draft CBDT Income-tax Rules 2026 'Rule 279' expanding the 50%-exemption metro list from 4 to 8 cities (adding Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad) for FY2026-27, but the sources reporting this explicitly label it 'Draft' as of publication and a direct fetch of the notified Rules (G.S.R. 198(E), 20 March 2026) could not locate the Rule 279 text to confirm finalisation. This pack conservatively keeps the confirmed 4-city list until the actual notified rule text is read — do not widen this to 8 cities without that confirmation.

regimes.old.section80dLimits.note: Limits unchanged (₹25,000/₹50,000 by age, self and parents; ₹1,00,000 combined max). Reported renumbered to Section 126 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 — corroborated by two independent secondary sources but NOT verified against the bare statute text directly; the rupee limits themselves are not in doubt.

houseProperty.standardDeductionRate.note: Section 22 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (replaces old Section 24) — carries the 30% standard deduction on house property annual value forward unchanged; corroborated by cleartax.in's description of the old Act's Section 24(a) mechanism (identical 30% figure, 'irrespective of actual expenditure'). Not available for a self-occupied property (nil annual value).

regimes.old.housePropertyLossSetOffCapAg.note: Old-regime cap of ₹2,00,000 on house-property loss set-off against other heads (Section 71(3A), IT Act 1961 -> Section 109(1)(b), Income-tax Act 2025 per TaxGuru's transition mapping); the rupee figure itself is unchanged by the renumbering.

regimes.new.housePropertyLossSetOffCapAg.note: New regime (115BAC / new-Act Section 202) disallows inter-head set-off of house-property loss entirely -- modelled as a ₹0 cap, not null (a loss genuinely exists, it just can't offset other heads this year).

old.actSection: Section 202 opt-out / Chapter equivalent (Income-tax Act, 2025) — old-regime computation continues as before under the new Act per incometax.gov.in guidance
